studies.label: Experiment 1 (vegetable-garden advice after real ChatGPT vs. Google search)

counts_source.quote: Participants were 1,136 membersa of the Prolific panel who were randomly assigned ... resulting in a final sample of 1,104 participants

arms.name: ChatGPT
arms.description: Participants could submit as many prompts as they wished through the in-house ChatGPT interface embedded in Qualtrics, then proceeded to write advice (PDF p. 3, Methods).

arms.name: Google
arms.description: Participants conducted actual Google searches through an in-house interface, browsing linked websites and submitting new queries as desired (PDF p. 3, Methods).

studies.task: Write advice to a friend on how to plant a vegetable garden, based on what was learned from the search

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-turbo; OpenAI Chat Completion API)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9, note c; PDF p. 3, Experiment 1, Methods. Model release year is not printed.

studies.label: Experiment 2 (vegetable-garden advice, information held constant, simulated ChatGPT vs. simulated Google)

counts_source.quote: Participants were 2,016 memberse of the Prolific panel who were randomly assigned ... We excluded 37 participants for failing an attention check, yielding a final sample of 1,979.

arms.name: ChatGPT (simulated)
arms.description: A fixed GPT-4o-generated summary was displayed in a simulated ChatGPT interface after a query; participants then proceeded to a separate page to write advice (PDF p. 6, Methods).

arms.name: Google (simulated)
arms.description: A simulated Google page linked to GPT-4o-generated article variants containing the same facts as the summary, with each article written in the style of a different media outlet (PDF p. 6, Methods).

studies.task: Write advice to a friend on how to plant a vegetable garden after the search task

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 6, Experiment 2, Methods. Model release year is not printed.

studies.label: Experiment 3 (healthier-lifestyle advice in the lab, Google standard vs. Google AI Overview; rated by Experiment 4 recipients)

counts_source.quote: Three participants were excluded for failing an attention check, leaving a final sample of 250

arms.name: Google LLM (AI Overview)
arms.description: Participants searched Google with the AI Overview extension installed and were instructed to read only its summary, without browsing the underlying links; they returned to the survey tab to write advice (PDF p. 7, Methods).

arms.name: Google standard
arms.description: Participants searched Google without the AI Overview extension and were instructed to browse the result links before returning to write advice (PDF p. 7, Methods).

studies.task: Write advice to a friend on how to lead a healthier lifestyle after searching

ai_tool.name: Google AI Overview (underlying model not named)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Experiment 3, Methods. Neither underlying model nor release year is printed.

preregistration.where: No writer-study preregistration is stated in PDF p. 7, Experiment 3, Methods. The later recipient evaluation is preregistered at https://aspredicted.org/6py8-ggdn.pdf (PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method).

estimates.outcome: Topical similarity of advice across writers (average pairwise cosine similarity)
estimates.measure_detail: LDA topic models fitted separately by condition; topic vectors reduced with PCA to equal dimensionality; average pairwise cosine similarity across all advice pairs within each condition. These are topic vectors, not neural embeddings (PDF p. 4, text-analysis methods).

estimates.notes: Question and outcome_with_ai are null: the paper describes writing after the search task but does not establish removal or continued availability of AI or source material during writing. The reconciled screening form leaves this classification unresolved; after_ai versus with_ai/across_people is not inferred from task order alone. Timing refers to when the writers produced their advice, in the same session as the search. The metric is computed over all pairs of advice within each condition (PDF p. 4, text-analysis methods). The paper does not establish the observation rows or aggregation used in its F test, or an adjustment for dependence among pairs. Accordingly unit and n_units are null and se_basis is unclear; degrees of freedom are not used to infer pair counts or participant-level uncertainty. The reported arm levels and F test are retained in the original metric.

estimates.outcome: Helpfulness of advice rated by recipients
estimates.measure_detail: Independent MTurk Connect recipients, blind to the source condition, rate one randomly selected text from each writer condition in randomized order. Item: "I find this advice very helpful". Agreement scale from strongly disagree to strongly agree (PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method).
estimates.notes: Question and outcome_with_ai are null: the paper describes writing after the search task but does not establish removal or continued availability of AI or source material during writing. The reconciled screening form leaves this classification unresolved; after_ai versus with_ai/across_people is not inferred from task order alone. Timing refers to when the writers produced their advice, in the same session as the search. Experiment 4 evaluates the advice produced by the Experiment 3 writers and is attached to S3. The reported repeated-measures ANOVA is across recipients, each of whom rates a sampled text from each writer condition. There is no reported adjustment for repeated ratings of the same writer text. within_person is null because writer assignment is between people, although recipient ratings are paired. n_total is null because the rating analysis does not separately enumerate the distinct randomized writers represented; recipient sample size is not substituted for a writer count. n_units is null because a total number of analyzed ratings is not printed. No outcome SD, SE, confidence interval, or standardized effect is printed.

estimates.outcome: Relative helpfulness of advice (side-by-side recipient choice)
estimates.measure_detail: Recipients compare a sampled pair of texts, one from each writer condition, and choose the more helpful one or a tie. Arm means below are the printed percentages choosing each source; the treatment-mean confidence interval is printed on the proportion scale (PDF p. 8, Experiment 4, Method and Results).

sources.quote: advice based on web links [24.6%, n = 367; 95% CI = (0.226, 0.271)]

estimates.notes: Question and outcome_with_ai are null: the paper describes writing after the search task but does not establish removal or continued availability of AI or source material during writing. The reconciled screening form leaves this classification unresolved; after_ai versus with_ai/across_people is not inferred from task order alone. Timing refers to when the writers produced their advice, in the same session as the search. This is an evaluation of S3 outputs, not a new AI-assigned writer sample. The printed condition labels are retained verbatim even though the article calls the LLM-labeled proportion significantly lower than the web-link proportion and concludes that LLM advice is less helpful. The labels contradict that interpretation; condition direction requires correction or labeled choice data. Mean fields contain percentages and CI fields contain the printed proportions; no conversion was performed. The control-mean interval and the choice counts are retained in the source quotations because the supplied stats structure has no control-mean CI or choice-count fields; choice counts are not per-arm writer counts. The chi-square test assesses equality of the choice proportions including ties, not a two-condition mean difference. The test treats recipient paired choices as independent and reports no adjustment for repeated use of writer texts; se_basis is pair. within_person is null because writer assignment is between people. n_total is null because distinct randomized writers represented in the choice analysis are not enumerated; n_units is null because the total number of analyzed pairs is not explicitly printed.

open_items: AI/source availability during advice writing is not established for S1-S3. Question and outcome_with_ai remain null pending instructions or access details; the paper establishes a later writing step but not removal of assistance.

No main-text output contrast reports arm SDs, arm SEs, contrast SEs, or standardized effects. No participant-level standardizer is transcribed or derived. Additional precision, if any, is in unavailable supplementary material or data.

Arm-level randomized and analyzed people counts are not printed for S1-S3. S3 reports recruitment separately from its analyzed total, without an explicit count at randomization; n_randomized stays null. The per-arm quantities given in Experiment 4 describe text pools and are not entered as people counts.

The diversity metrics compare all within-condition pairs, but the observations, aggregation, and dependence adjustment behind the reported F tests are unspecified. Unit and n_units remain null and se_basis remains unclear.

Recipient-based uncertainty in the S3 output evaluations does not account for repeated ratings or choices involving the same writers. The article does not enumerate distinct writers represented in the recipient analyses or print total numbers of ratings/pairs. No rater-based precision is treated as participant-level writer precision.

Relative-helpfulness choice labels conflict with the narrative direction on PDF p. 8. Retain printed labels and obtain corrected labels or condition-labeled choice data before interpreting the effect.

The supplementary replications S5-S7 cannot be extracted exhaustively from the brief main-text descriptions. The separate supplement was not local; Europe PMC fullTextXML and the PMC Open Access API both failed with WinError 10013 during retrieval.
Countries are not stated for S1-S3. S3 is described as a university behavioral-lab panel, but student status and population composition are not established.
Tool release years are not printed, and the model underlying Google AI Overview is not named. These fields are not inferred from general product knowledge.

The main paper identifies preregistrations for S1, S2, and the recipient study but does not name a preregistered primary creative-output outcome; primary-outcome status remains not_stated. No preregistration is stated for S3 writers.
notes: Read the entire local markdown conversion through the final reference. All cited PDF pages were extracted with PyMuPDF and checked; the PDF contains no appended supplementary section or embedded files. The extraction contains the three main randomized writer samples. The recipient evaluation reuses S3 advice and does not create a further AI-assigned writer sample; no cross-paper participant overlap is stated. Both content conditions in S2 use GPT-4o-generated material, so their comparison is ai_design. The current codebook categories length and text_features are used for the word and named-entity counts, respectively. Unknown question classification is retained as null consistently with the reconciled screening form. Numeric values are transcribed without computing differences, effects, standard errors, arm counts, pair counts, or ratings totals; source quotes preserve printed precision, including trailing zeros. Quotes normalize whitespace and remove discretionary line-break hyphens; ellipses in study count quotes mark noncontiguous excerpts from the same page. The scale for the recipient ratings is documented in PDF p. 8: on a scale of 1 = “Strongly disagree” to 5 = “Strongly agree”: The supplementary publisher link is http://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgaf316#supplementary-data (PDF p. 10). In-memory retrieval attempts used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifiers: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12560091/fullTextXML and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi?id=PMC12560091. Both were denied by socket permissions; no supplementary content was obtained. PDF p. 10 names OSF for relevant data, surveys, and preregistrations but supplies no usable repository identifier or URL.
